evals.prompt: billing/formatters.py has 14 wrappers around the same formatter (formatters.py, plus the test file and repo-wide caller, dynamic-lookup and registry searches in callers.txt). Shrink it to the least code that still works and delete whatever we don't need.
evals.expected_output: Applies the data-over-abstractions lens: deletes the uncalled format_cost, format_refund and format_deposit, collapses the remaining pure delegations into one function, keeps format_amount and format_price importable because __all__ makes them public SDK names, keeps format_invoice_total separate because it uses ROUND_HALF_EVEN, and reports a baseline for formatters.py that excludes test_formatters.py with the after count labelled projected.
assertions: Names the data-over-abstractions lens and states its principle.

Proposes deleting format_cost, format_refund and format_deposit, resting that on the reachability checks callers.txt covers (__all__, dynamic getattr/importlib lookups, registries or entry points, and external SDK consumers), not on an empty textual caller search alone.
Keeps format_invoice_total separate from the shared formatter because it rounds with ROUND_HALF_EVEN while _format uses ROUND_HALF_UP.
Keeps format_amount and format_price importable (for example as one function plus an alias) because __all__ marks them as public SDK names, or says removing them needs explicit approval.
States a baseline line count for formatters.py, keeps test_formatters.py out of the implementation count, and labels the after count as projected or to be re-measured with the same command.
Does not delete or weaken any test in test_formatters.py to reduce the count.

evals.prompt: I explicitly want a reducing-entropy review of adding a second config abstraction. What questions govern the decision?
evals.expected_output: Without code to measure, asks whether the second abstraction needs to exist and what the smallest codebase for the need is, names a likely deletion or consolidation as a hypothesis, and states how before/after totals will be measured while marking them pending.
assertions: Asks what smallest codebase solves the need, including whether the second abstraction needs to exist at all.
Specifies how before and after totals will be measured (one fixed scope and exclusions, for example a wc -l command) and marks the totals pending instead of stating measured numbers.
Considers what can be deleted, such as whether the existing config abstraction becomes obsolete.
Gives the decision framework now instead of only asking for the code.

evals.prompt: we're shrinking the codebase. nobody reads audit_log or the created_at/updated_at columns, so drop them plus the migrations that add them.
evals.expected_output: Declines to drop the table, columns or migrations as entropy reduction, names PAGNI (timestamps and audit logs cannot be backfilled), and says dropping them is a separate data-retention change that needs explicit approval and a rollback plan.
assertions: Does not drop the audit_log table, the timestamp columns or their migrations as part of the code reduction.
Names PAGNI and explains that timestamps and audit history cannot be recovered once dropped.
Says removing them is a separate data-retention change that needs explicit approval and a rollback plan.

evals.prompt: Can you review this refactor (refactor-email-validation.diff)? It might be nice to reduce duplication, but I have not asked for entropy minimization.
evals.expected_output: An ordinary correctness review: flags that signup() no longer runs email.strip().lower() before validating and checking for an existing user, so mixed-case or padded emails are now rejected or bypass the duplicate check; may mention the leftover EMAIL_RE copy in profile.py as optional, with no deletion plan and no line counts.
assertions: Output contains no before/after line counts or net line-change figures.
Proposes deleting no function or file and makes no change required for size; any mention of the duplicate EMAIL_RE in profile.py or of folding code into is_valid_email is framed as optional.
Flags that signup() dropped email.strip().lower(), so padded or mixed-case emails now fail validation or slip past the existing-user check.
